title: Diagnostic packet
description: The one record `diagnose` publishes at the end of a run, through the knowledgebase adapter's `publishArtifact` under a `run-artifact` placement: the symptom as reported, the feedback loop, the minimised reproduction, the ranked hypotheses, the causal chain and the summary, plus exactly one of the run's two outputs. `patch` describes a verified bounded patch written under a grant that covers it and left in the workspace; `packet` points at the diagnostic work packet, a `ticket` in the work-packet shape, where no grant covered the fix. Never both: a packet that names a patch this run already applied is both outputs wearing one name, and the second reader implements the same change twice (ruling `diagnose-patch-or-packet-never-both`, docs/decisions/0001-kb-document-vocabulary.md §3). Receipts are `verification` artifacts referenced here, never restated: an account of a green run is not one (ruling `closure-requires-independent-verification`). This record closes nothing.

symptom.description: The reported symptom, verbatim as the reporter stated it, recorded before anything runs. A symptom re-described by the diagnosing run is a different bug from the one that was reported. Secrets are written as <REDACTED>.

source_revision.description: Narrowed from the envelope: the revision being diagnosed, recorded before anything runs. Evidence with no revision to bind it to is evidence nobody can re-check, so null is not admissible.

loop.description: The red-capable feedback loop: one command, already run at least once, that goes red on this bug and would go green once it is fixed, with the receipt of it going red.

reproduction.description: The minimised reproduction: every remaining input, caller, configuration item and step is load-bearing.

hypotheses.description: Three to five, ranked, written before any was tested, each with the prediction it makes. A hypothesis with no prediction is discarded or sharpened, not ranked lower.

prediction.description: If this is the cause, then changing that makes the failure go away.

evidence.description: The probe receipts that confirmed or disconfirmed it.

causal_chain.description: Written in full before asking anything about what to do with it: the trigger, each step and the observed symptom, each with its location.

grant.description: The grant decision, recorded either way: whether a grant covered the files the fix touches. Absence of a grant narrows what is written, never what is investigated.

patch.description: A verified bounded patch, left in the workspace for the lane that owns integration; this skill commits nothing. It carries the regression test, or the recorded absence of a correct seam, and the receipts from the red step, the green step and the re-run of the original unminimised reproduction.

files.description: The files the change touches, all within the grant.

regression_test.description: Written before the fix, at a seam that exercises the bug as it occurs at the call site.

seam_absent.description: Where no correct seam exists, that is the finding, and the feedback loop carries the evidence a test would have carried.

packet.description: The diagnostic work packet: a `ticket` in the work-packet shape, with acceptance criteria, named verification bound to those criteria, a bounded write scope and an integration owner, specified well enough to be implemented once. It carries this record's reproduction, hypotheses and causal chain with it.

architecture_question.description: Where the fix attempts ran out or a runner budget was exhausted: what the failures have in common, stated as an architecture question rather than a fourth attempt.

summary.description: The same summary either way. The confidence is advisory, says how sure this run is and closes nothing (ruling `closure-requires-independent-verification`).

should_have_caught.description: The tests that should have caught it.

change.description: What was changed, or why nothing was.

reason.description: On needs-input, what was tried and what would unblock it; on failed, why. Never a hypothesis reached without a loop.

allOf.description: A patch or a packet, never both.
No hypothesis before a red-capable loop exists.
A patch is written only under a grant that covers it.
The packet carries the minimised reproduction, the ranked hypotheses and the causal chain with its locations.
A complete run emitted exactly one output, recorded the grant decision, and returns the summary.
At the cap the diagnosis is handed on as a packet with the architecture question stated, not a fourth attempt.
A run that stops short says what was tried and what would unblock it, or why it failed.
